# Chapter 2: Workflow Basics
## Coding basics

- You can use R for basic math calculations
- You can create new objects with the assignment operator `<-`, which can be easily entered using the keyboard shortcut `⌥-`.
- You can combine multiple elements into a vector with `c()` (think c = concatenate or combine).
- You can apply basic arithmetic to every element of the vector.

## Comments
`#` allows you to write comments, which will make your code more readable. Use comments to explain the *why* of code, not the how or what. Those are always possible to figure out, but the why is more difficult!

## What's in a name?
Posit recommends `snake_case` rather than `camelCase`.
```{r}
this_is_a_really_long_name <- 2.5
```
- You can use other keyboard shortcuts.
    - `↑` brings you to the last command you typed so you can edit it.
    - Typing "this" then pressing `Cmd + ↑` lists all th commands you've typed that starts with the letters "this".
- You have to be precise in your instructions. No typos and consistent case throughout.

## Calling functions

R has a lot of functions that are called like this:

```{r}
#| eval: false
function_name(argument1 = value, argument2 = value2, ...)
```

For example, `seq()` makes regular sequences of numbers.

```{r}
seq(from = 1, to = 10)
seq(1, 10)
```

We can omit the names of the first several arguments in function calls, so the above functions do the same thing.
